ledger.claim: The detour was not rider-requested. All three chat messages carry waypoint_hint = null and the rider names no road, so POL-RD-04's 200 m corroboration test is undecidable on the record and the clause is unavailable. In any event the messages show a rider questioning the route ('hello why we going towards city centre? MBS is the other side') and a driver admitting fault ('sorry boss missed the exit, coming back now') — there is no instruction anywhere in the log that could exonerate the excess.

Nothing resets the 21.0 km baseline. vehicle_type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12's matched-itinerary baseline does not apply and there is no co-rider distance to exclude; and pickup_amended_at, dropoff_amended_at and amended_optimal_distance_km are all null, so there is no POL-RD-05 relocation recomputation to run. The measured excess of 6.18 km stands unreduced.

The trace is clean and unimpaired for policy purposes: 229 fixes at a 10 s sample interval, 100% coverage, max_gap_sec of 0.0 and an empty gaps array, so POL-RD-07(a)-(c) do not fire and no independent corroboration is required to establish the deviation. Even if it were, the driver's own chat admission supplies it.

The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged. trip_id TRP-00101 and the pickup timestamp match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown, and limb (b) is met because the excess clears the POL-RD-01 threshold on an unimpaired trace. The burden therefore shifts to the driver, who has pointed to no specific exculpatory artifact and no clause to displace the finding.

POL-RD-09 adds nothing to the refund and must not be double-counted against it. The fare_breakdown lists no erp_gantries and carries optimal_route_erp of 0.0, and the trip does not originate at an airport, so there is no off-route ERP, toll or surcharge pass-through correction to stack on top of the POL-RD-02 figure. The rider's recovery is the distance-and-time recomputation alone.

The rider is the filing party, so under the party-relative rule of POL-GEN-03 NO_ACTION would leave the $35.64 charge standing against her. The rider-favouring outcome is the partial refund, which strips out the $8.05 that the driver's admitted wrong turn added to a trip that should have cost 27.63.

The route deviation is established but falls well short of MATERIAL. On the governing trace the trip ran 27.18 km against a booked optimal of 21.0 km, an excess of 6.18 km (29.4%). That passes POL-RD-01's two establishment tests (greater than 0.8 km and greater than 20%) but is below BOTH materiality gates (greater than 8.0 km and greater than 50%). The deviation is therefore non-material, so the driver_profile check in POL-RD-06 is not even engaged, no FULL_REFUND uplift is available and the remedy is capped at the POL-RD-02 arithmetic partial.

The distance must be measured on the trace. POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km = 27.18 km (EV-GPS-00101) govern over trip_record.actual_distance_km = 27.2 km (EV-TRIP-00101), which is a rounded convenience copy that may not be cited for the threshold test. On the governing field the excess is 6.18 km, exactly as the derived block computes, so the establishment finding stands on a clean, unimpaired 100%-coverage trace with no gaps and a 10 s sample interval - this is not a POL-RD-07 impaired-trace case and no independent corroboration is required.

No repeat-deviation pattern can be established against this driver. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 812 completed_trips_90d (EV-DPROF-00101), which fails POL-RD-06's tests (3 or more flags, or a ratio of 0.05 or more). Combined with the non-material excess, POL-RD-06 is not triggered on any limb: there is no FULL_REFUND uplift, no evidence re-weighing, and no driver-conduct referral.

Whatever refund issues is arithmetic under POL-RD-02 and cannot exceed SGD 8.05. The fare is METERED (EV-FARE-00101.fare_model), so POL-RD-02 governs and POL-RD-11 does not. On the booked optimal of 21.0 km / 26.0 min at surge 1.0: (3.80 + 0.75 x 21.0 + 0.28 x 26.0) = 26.83, plus the 0.80 platform fee = 27.63 recomputed_fare. Refund = 35.64 charged_total - 27.63 = 8.01, rounded UP to SGD 8.05. That is 22.6% of charged_total, so it is a PARTIAL_REFUND, not the FULL_REFUND the rider asks for, and it is well below the SGD 10.00 contested amount.

The only direct evidence of fault is the driver's own contemporaneous in-app message (EV-CHAT-00101, 'sorry boss missed the exit, coming back now'), which describes a simple navigational error corrected within the trip, not a deliberate detour. That is consistent with a single non-material excess and gives no foothold for the POL-RD-06(b) full-refund uplift or the POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral.

ruling.explanation:
Both of you: the dispute is a route deviation on TRP-00101 (Jurong East to Marina Bay Sands) and it resolves as a partial refund.

THE DEVIATION IS ESTABLISHED. POL-RD-01 measures actual distance on the GPS trace, and the trace (EV-GPS-00101) records 27.18 km against the booked optimal of 21.0 km — an excess of 6.18 km, or 29.4%. That clears both establishment tests (more than 0.8 km absolute and more than 20% of optimal). The 27.2 km figure on the trip record is a rounded convenience copy and is not the figure the threshold test runs on. Both parties agree on this, and I accept it.

IT IS NOT A MATERIAL DEVIATION. 6.18 km is below the 8.0 km gate and 29.4% is below the 50% gate, so POL-RD-06 is not triggered: no profile-based re-weighing of the evidence, no full-refund uplift, and no driver-conduct referral. The driver's point here is correct, and the rider's claim for the full contested amount is not supported.

NO EXCULPATION APPLIES. There is no traffic advisory for the AYE/MCE/ECP corridor in the record, so POL-RD-03 cannot be run. There is no rider instruction in the chat log — all three messages carry no waypoint hint and name no road — so POL-RD-04 is unavailable. There is no pickup or dropoff amendment (POL-RD-05) and the vehicle is RYDE_X, not a pooled trip (POL-RD-12). The driver's own in-app message, 'sorry boss missed the exit, coming back now', is an admission of a navigational error and not a defence; no exculpatory clause survives.

THE REFUND IS ARITHMETIC (POL-RD-02):
- charged_total: SGD 35.64
- recomputed_fare: SGD 27.63 — ((3.80 + 0.75 x 21.0 + 0.28 x 26.0) x 1.0 surge) + 0.80 platform fee; the surge multiplier of 1.0 is read from EV-FARE-00101.surge_multiplier, with no on-optimal-route ERP, no surcharge, no waiting fee and no promo.
- refund: SGD 8.05 — 35.64 less 27.63 = 8.01, rounded UP to the nearest 5 cents.

This is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and well below 90% of the charge, so it is a PARTIAL_REFUND, not the full refund the rider asks for. No ERP, toll or surcharge line exists on this fare, so nothing is added on top and nothing is double-counted under POL-RD-09. No bogus gantry or misplaced airport surcharge appears, so no billing-integrity referral arises, and no clause produces any other referral.

ON CONFIDENCE: every artifact the ruling rests on — the GPS trace, the trip record and the fare breakdown — carries full weight 1.0, and both advocates agree on the arithmetic, so confidence is high at 0.92, above the platform floor.

The rider's original argument that the absent LTA advisory settles the closure question was not admitted because it cited the missing artifact without disclosing its impairment, but the outcome is the same: no closure defence is available on this record either way.
